column17: Paper 'proposes a shopfloor layout generation method based on Prompt Engineering' (abstract): designs an artifact (information metamodel, prompt templates, RAG knowledge units, think-generate-evaluate iteration) and evaluates it on case experiments, an in-house Q&A dataset and an ablation study (Sections 3-4).
column19: Working system (Mixtral 8x7B deployed locally, temperature 0.5; JSON parser + THREEJS 3D rendering) plus quantitative evaluation: Q&A accuracy for four LLMs (Fig. 11), comparison vs CoT baseline on space utilization/compliance/layout-pattern/constraint metrics (Table 2), ablation study (Table 3).
column20: Discrete manufacturing (metal-parts machining shopfloor); Q&A dataset sources include motor manufacturing plants and textile companies
column21: Small discrete manufacturing shopfloor with one production line for metal parts, equipped with CNC lathes, CNC milling machines, drilling machines and inspection tables; layout patterns tested: double-line (I-shape), L-shape, U-shape (Section 4.2)
column22: NR (no explicit RQs; stated aim: 'refine and decompose the complex problem of shopfloor layout by leveraging the integrative and creative potential of large language models' and 'systematically explore the effects of different dimensional problems on the generation results of LLMs', p. 285)
column24: Task is shopfloor (equipment) layout design - the layout-planning step of factory planning. Boundary case: authors target 'enterprises that frequently need to adjust production lines or equipment layouts' and 'scenarios where production conditions ... often change' (p. 297), i.e. re-layout/reconfiguration, which leans tactical; no supply-chain, site or technology-selection content.
column29: No time horizon stated. Layout design is classically a structural/strategic factory-planning task, but the paper frames applicability as flexible shopfloors that 'frequently need to adjust production lines or equipment layouts' with changing 'product types and process flows' (p. 297), suggesting recurring re-layout (upper-tactical). Classified ambiguous; R1 decision needed.
column31: The decision determines the spatial configuration of the shopfloor: 'to determine the positioning and arrangement of these elements, considering shape constraints, size limitations, and the topological relationships between their spatial positions' (p. 289); output is equipment positions/rotations within the layout space (JSON, Fig. 2). Equipment set is given; the decision configures placement, not the equipment inventory. Not explicitly labelled 'system-configuring' by the authors.
column33: Richard Muther's Systematic Layout Planning (SLP) cited in the introduction as the 'most classic approach' (p. 284); not used as the paper's own framework. Could alternatively be coded 'none'.
column34: LLM generates 2D shopfloor equipment layouts (equipment positions/rotations, JSON per an information metamodel) from a structured prompt template Task={Role, Space, Factory, Request} plus output prompt (examples, structure hints) and RAG-retrieved knowledge units KnowU=<E,R> about equipment (geometric, textual, constraint models). Generation runs in an iterative 'thinking-generation-evaluation' chain (CoT/ReAct-inspired) with re-retrieval when knowledge is missing and expert evaluation/guidance; results are parsed and rendered as 3D scenes (THREEJS, GLTF model base) for planners/decision-makers. Inputs: equipment information, layout space, layout requirements (layout pattern); outputs: layout scheme.
column36: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, ChatGLM3-6B and Mixtral 8x7B compared on the spatial-reasoning Q&A dataset (Section 4.1, Fig. 11). Mixtral 8x7B, locally deployed with temperature 0.5, used for the layout generation method validation, CoT comparison and ablation (Section 4.2).
column38: ChatGLM (ChatGLM3-6B, Zhipu AI / Tsinghua KEG Laboratory)
column40: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 proprietary; Mixtral 8x7B ('open weights', p. 296) and ChatGLM3-6B open-weight. The layout-generation method itself was validated only with open-weight Mixtral 8x7B ('open-source large language model Mixtral 8x7B for local deployment', p. 297).
column42: No weight updates; method 'mainly utilizes the generalized capability of the large language model without deeper downstream task adaptation training' (p. 299). Fine-tuning on layout scenario cases named as future work.
column51: The paper situates itself against the facility-layout OR tradition (SLP-based mathematical models solved with GA, PSO, simulated annealing; RL-based layout planning per Klar et al.) but uses no solver or formal objective: 'generative methods are not directly comparable to traditional approaches' (p. 298). Layout elements are formalized as axis-parallel rectangles in a 2D coordinate system (Fig. 5) with comprehensive (boundary) and relational (inter-equipment) constraints; quality is measured post hoc via space utilization, compliance, layout-pattern fulfilment and constraint satisfaction. Uncertainty: 'present' refers to the acknowledged domain tradition, not to an optimization component in the system; R1 may prefer FALSE/none.

column53: Proprietary in-house Q&A dataset, 340 questions in four categories (absolute/relative position 57, coordinate transformation 85, spatial relationship 107, circumstances 91; Table 1), built from enterprise documents of motor manufacturing plants and textile companies; not publicly available. column113: All four LLMs showed high accuracy on the spatial-reasoning Q&A set; GPT-4 clearly outperformed the others and the small open-weight Mixtral 8x7B performed 'surprisingly well'. Incomplete/ambiguous task descriptions increased hallucination. In the layout case study with Mixtral 8x7B, the proposed method roughly doubled space utilization vs CoT (e.g. 0.602 vs 0.261 at 10 elements) and substantially raised layout-pattern fulfilment and comprehensive/relational constraint satisfaction, while compliance stayed similar; the advantage persisted as element count grew (8-15). Ablation showed constraint representation is critical for constraint satisfaction (0.013 without it) and question decomposition/coordinate mapping prevents random or over-concentrated placement. Failure modes: tight spacing, overlaps, out-of-boundary placement, interference (Fig. 12).
column116: In each think-generate-evaluate cycle the evaluation step is to 'evaluate ... the generated layout and make manual decisions, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the generated layout and guidance for necessary adjustments' (p. 293; Fig. 9 'Decision-making + LLMs Assessment'). Experts familiar with prompt engineering 'continue to give appropriate layout knowledge and prompts for guidance' during generation (p. 298); authors state the 'need for expert involvement during generation' (p. 299). Also manual supplementary evaluation of Q&A answers. Pattern is iterative expert review and steering rather than a pure pre-execution approval gate; could be coded 'other'.
column120: Shopfloor 'information metamodel' (UML-style class model, Fig. 1) with three levels (shopfloor, production line unit, equipment) and typed attributes (basic info, geometric info, comprehensive and relationship constraints), instantiated as JSON with DTDL-style identifiers ('dtmi:com:XXX:Equipment;1', Fig. 2). Equipment knowledge abstracted into three models (mathematical, text-information, constraint; Fig. 6) and encoded as knowledge units KnowU=<E,R> (elements + semantic/constraint relations) retrieved via Word2vec/cosine-similarity RAG. Not called an ontology by the authors; KnowU=<E,R> is knowledge-graph-like - R1 may prefer 'knowledge-graph' or 'other'.
column124: Layout quality metrics defined by the authors: completeness/compliance, space utilization, comprehensive-constraint and relational-constraint satisfaction, and layout-pattern (I/L/U-shape) fulfilment (p. 298, Table 2). Additionally an in-house 340-question spatial-reasoning Q&A dataset with rule-based and manual scoring serves as an LLM capability benchmark (Table 1, Fig. 11). Metric computation formulas are not given.
column127: Key steps are described (metamodel, prompt template structure, RAG via Word2vec/cosine similarity, think-generate-evaluate loop, model and temperature, iteration limits) but replication gaps remain: full prompt texts, metric computation formulas (space utilization, compliance, constraint scores), the Q&A dataset (proprietary, not public), Fig. 11 numeric values and code are not provided; 'these operations are standard practices within the RAG framework ... briefly summarized here without in-depth discussion' (p. 292).
column129: Implemented system (Mixtral 8x7B locally deployed, parser, THREEJS rendering) with quantitative evaluation: Q&A accuracy of four LLMs (Fig. 11), comparison vs CoT baseline across element counts and layout patterns (Table 2), and ablation study (Table 3); single developer-defined case, no external benchmark.
